newsitem.title: USA: SNYDER SAYS SOME OF AMOCO SALE OF INTEREST.
newsitem.headline: SNYDER SAYS SOME OF AMOCO SALE OF INTEREST.

text.p: Snyder Oil Corp chairman John Snyder told a conference call after second quarter earnings that some properties in Wyoming and the Rocky Mountains being sold by Amoco Corp would be of interest.

Amoco announced in June that it would sell some 15 percent of its U.S. reserves and Snyder said earlier this week that following the spinoff of its Patina Oil & Gas Corp unit, the sale of stakes in two London-listed subsidiaries and a bank credit line, it planned to spend $400-$600 million on acquisitions.
"The perception is that these (Amoco properties) are larger, more quality properties," said Snyder.
He also said that Patina may be interested in some of the Wattenberg properties that Amoco is selling, which underly its own producing properties.
"Patina is being spun off at same time as Amoco is looking to put wattenberg on the market, that is kind of interesting for all of us to watch," Snyder said.

Snyder Oil said that output from its core properties in Louisiana, the Gulf of Mexico and the Rockies would mean that the company is on target to increase core production by 5--10 percent this year and that by the middle of next year, output should be close the the level it was before the Patina spinoff.

Including Patina, production is 41,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, that will fall to 23,000 after the spinoff, but the company projects that it will be back at 36,000 boe per day by the middle of next year.
"The big kicker in 1998 will be the Main Pass platform," said Rick Wollen, vice president corporate development. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
